# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

# Decouple the storyline doc-drift guard from engine-owned heading text

**Headline:** `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` AC5b pins literal Markdown headings of the engine-owned reference `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (a git submodule that dev builds advance to the engine's latest dev tip), so any engine-side heading rename silently reddens this game's unit suite. Replace the heading pins with semantic anchors (API symbols, link resolution) plus a rename-tolerant section-structure check, and document why headings are not a cross-repo contract.

discovered-from: MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L

## Problem statement

Dev builds (`npm run build` → `engine:sync`) compose the **latest** engine dev tip via `git submodule update --remote core`, not the pinned release SHA. When core (dev tip `01d6bcc1`) renamed `## Engine adapter` → `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` in `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, the game's doc-drift guard (AC5b) reddened on **every** dev build, for **every** game repo that pins those headings — even though nothing in Main Street changed. The inline fix (commit `9f2c6185`) asserted the new heading, but the underlying coupling remains: a heading is an implementation detail of the engine's prose, not a contract the game depends on.

## Users / user stories

- As a **Main Street developer**, when I bump or dev-sync the engine, I want `npm test` to fail only for genuine breakage, so a green suite is trustworthy and a red suite means something real.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the doc guard to still fail loudly if the engine reference the game's adapters link to disappears or stops documenting the seam API, so releases cannot silently ship against vanished docs.
- As the **producer/operator**, I want the cross-repo doc dependency to be explicit and cheap to maintain, so a rename is a no-op (or a documented one-line change), not a cross-repo firefight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No literal engine heading pins.** The AC5b block in `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` no longer asserts literal section-heading text of `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`; instead it asserts the semantic anchors the game genuinely depends on: the core reference exists, documents `createStorylineSystem` and the `@story-line` package, and names the `GymStorylineScene` consumer (any of these removed → guard fails).
- **AC2 — Rename tolerance is proven by a fixture test.** A new unit test in the same file feeds a fixture copy of the core doc with section headings renamed (e.g. `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` → `## Renamed seam section`) and asserts the contract check still passes; a negative fixture (missing `createStorylineSystem`) asserts the check still fails. *Metric: run the two fixture cases — tolerance passes, regression fails.*
- **AC3 — Link resolution preserved.** The guard keeps asserting that `docs/game/storylines.md` links to `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and that the target resolves on disk, and that the core reference is linked from `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `core/docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`.
- **AC4 — Failure messages and rationale.** Any guard failure names the offending file and the missing anchor, and the test header comment explains that engine doc headings are not a cross-repo contract and cites this work item (`MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O`); a corresponding one-line note is added near the "thin adapters" paragraph of `docs/game/storylines.md` and under the `## Tests` heading in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` so the next engineer does not re-pin headings. *Metric: a reading of the header comment + both doc notes shows the work-item id and the "headings are not a contract" statement.*
- **AC5 — Engine-revision tolerant and suite green.** The changed test scope passes with the submodule at the pinned SHA and with the engine dev tip the build composes; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- Game-side change only — do **not** edit files inside `core/` (engine-owned submodule, re-scaffolded by the game-repo scaffold); if an engine-side fix is later chosen, it is an engine-repo (CG) work item.
- Do not weaken the guard into a no-op: negative cases (missing file, missing symbol, broken link) must still fail the suite.
- No new dependencies; keep the guard in plain vitest + `node:fs`, consistent with the file's existing style.
- Do not change `configs/engine-pin.json` or the `core` gitlink as part of this work (they already agree at dev HEAD: pin `40f83b986a6578b3887dcda8857dd5ee7aa15e57` == gitlink `40f83b98`, re-pinned by commit `5b2ddf72`; the pair moves together on every dev build, so treat the exact SHA as illustrative, not a constant).

## Existing state

- Guard: `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, AC5b block asserts `['## API', '## Authoring seams', '## UI adapter', '## Gym demo']` against `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (created by MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY / MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR; heading pin baked in by commit `9f2c6185`).
- Engine doc at current pin (`40f83b98`) has sections: API, Validation, Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author), Editor (visual authoring tool), Engine adapter, UI adapter, Gym demo, Testing. Note both `## Authoring seams …` and `## Engine adapter` exist at this revision — proof that pinning either name is fragile; the guard must not depend on heading text at all.
- The engine repo currently has **no** docs-consistency test and **no** heading anchor manifest (verified: no engine tests reference `docs/core-engine`, no anchor file) — so "engine owns the contract" would be net-new engine work.
- Sibling churn pattern already fixed inline: MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (pin/pointer mismatch when dev sync advances the submodule during a build).

## Desired change

1. Refactor the AC5b assertions into a small pure helper `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc: string, headers: {file: string; link: boolean}): string[]` (returns missing anchors), so the same logic runs against the real file and against fixtures.
2. Replace the `['## API', …]` heading pins with: file-exists + `createStorylineSystem`/`@story-line`/`GymStorylineScene` presence + a structural check that the doc "documents the section topics" without pinning exact heading text (e.g. each required topic keyword found somewhere in the doc, tolerant of heading renames).
3. Add fixture-driven tests for rename tolerance (pass) and missing-symbol regression (fail).
4. Update the test header comment + the two doc notes (AC4).

## Implementation plan (single vertical slice)

This is a **leaf `task`**, not an epic: one test file plus two one-line doc notes. It is
small enough (effort `Small`, risk `Medium`) that phasing adds ceremony without value, so it is
implemented as a **single vertical slice** (code/guard + tests + docs in one change set) rather
than decomposed into child work items. Within that slice the order preserves test-first
verification: the new contract check is written so its tolerance/regression fixtures fail before
the old heading pins are removed, then the pins are replaced, then the docs notes land.

1. Extract the AC5b assertions into `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc, headers)` returning a
   list of missing anchors (pure, no `fs` inside) — AC1 groundwork, keeps the real-file and
   fixture paths on the same logic.
2. Add the fixture tests first and watch them fail against the current heading-pinned helper:
   renamed-heading fixture passes, `createStorylineSystem`-missing fixture fails — AC2.
3. Replace the `['## API', …]` pins with file-exists + `createStorylineSystem` / `@story-line` /
   `GymStorylineScene` + rename-tolerant section-topic check, calling the helper — AC1, AC3.
4. Update the header comment and the two doc notes with the work-item id — AC4.
5. Verify with the changed-scope test run at the current checkout, then the full suite — AC5.
6. Finish with the standard implementation close-out (build → test → commit in that order).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — AC5b block rewrite, tolerance/regression fixture tests, header rationale.
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/storyline-core-doc-renamed-heading.md` (new) — fixture mirroring the current core doc with headings renamed; or an inline string fixture to avoid duplicating a 400-line doc. Prefer the smallest fixture that provably exercises the renames; if inline, note that it must be refreshed on engine doc content changes.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — one-line note that the guard asserts semantic anchors, not engine heading text.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — one-line note under "Tests" about the engine-doc heading non-contract.
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` gitlink — read-only references; must not be edited here.

## Related work

- MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR — created AC5b ("Storyline docs and drift guards", completed).
- MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY — canonical docs + doc-drift guard (completed).
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — browser-wait soak child where this was discovered (completed).
- MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F — sibling pin/pointer churn from dev-sync submodule advance (completed) — same root-cause class.
- MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV — open sibling that makes the composed engine explicit and fails when worktree `./core` lags the pin (complementary: this item makes the guard tolerant of the composed engine's docs).
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED — origin of dev-sync-on-build policy (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** the more thorough option — "the cross-repo doc contract should be owned by the engine (stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest)" — is deliberately **out of scope** here: it is net-new engine (CG) work affecting every game repo, and it is a producer decision. It is recorded as an open question in the Appendix; if approved, file a separate CG work item. This item stays game-side and is a prerequisite/valid regardless of that decision.
- **Assumption:** semantic symbols (`createStorylineSystem`, `@story-line`, `GymStorylineScene`) are stable markers of the seam API the game links to; the tolerance fixture must keep the renamed headings under the current section topics so it stays representative.
- **Risk — over-loosening:** a rename-tolerant check can drift into a no-op. Mitigated by AC2's negative fixture and AC3's link-resolution assertions.

# Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect

**Headline:** The Main Street story-line engine adapter omits the core `applyResourceDelta` seam, so option `cost` and `extraEffect` are never charged or applied.

Discovered-from: `MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY` (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Problem

Core `@story-line` resolves an option's declarative `cost` and `extraEffect` through the engine adapter's optional `applyResourceDelta` seam (`core/src/story-line/resolve.ts`). A legacy adapter without it is left untouched and appends the activity-log line *"Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied: the engine adapter does not implement applyResourceDelta."*

`mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts`) implements `rng`, `applyEffect`, `getResources`, `appendLog`, `getActivityLog`, `getTemplate`, `getBaseTypeId`, `getChainScanCards` and `pushChainCard` — but **not** `applyResourceDelta`.

Consequences:

- A cost-gated option is filtered out of the presented list at draw time (`isOptionAffordable`), yet a *presented* cost option is never actually charged — so affordability never changes after paying.
- `extraEffect` deltas silently never land (options are inert where content expects a bonus/penalty).
- Any card using a cost or extra effect pollutes the activity log with the warning line above.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, the AI cost-aware policy (`MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY`) scores costs that the engine never collects and effects that never apply. The AI unit contract can still be satisfied (projection is a pure function), but end-to-end play with cost-bearing options is incorrect.

Secondary gap (same story, narrower): CSV `options` authoring has no syntax for `cost`/`extraEffect`, and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` `#/definitions/option` carries only `label`/`successorIds`/`effectPolicy`. So content cannot yet declare a cost — only registered options can. Authoring support should be its own item once enforcement exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` implements `applyResourceDelta(state, delta)`, applying `coins` and `reputation` deltas to `state.resourceBank` and keeping the ledger/score view consistent (same sync path `resolveEventOption` uses, e.g. `syncResourceBankToLedger`).
- A unit test proves a cost-bearing option deducts exactly `cost.coins`/`cost.reputation` on resolution, for both `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and `'skip'`.
- A unit test proves `extraEffect` deltas are applied for both effect policies, and that the resolution result's `coinChange`/`repChange` reports cost + extra effect + (for `apply`) the card effect.
- An integration test resolves a pending cost choice headlessly and asserts the activity log contains **no** "Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied" line.
- Undo of a resolved paid choice (snapshot command) restores the pre-payment resources; save/load round-trip preserves the post-payment balance.
- Existing behaviour with cost-free options is unchanged (storyline regression harness green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter, delegating to the existing state resource helpers and the ledger sync one-liner.
- Follow the settlement order documented in core: card effect (per `effectPolicy`) → cost → extra effect.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts` — add `applyResourceDelta`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` settlement/ledger sync + log assertions
- `src/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank` and ledger sync helpers
- `core/src/story-line/resolve.ts` — settlement order and warning contract (read-only)
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts` — resolution test home

## Notes

- `core/` is a pinned submodule — no core changes expected; if core needs a signature change, raise it as a core (`CG-`) item instead.

`npm run build` runs `engine:sync`, which advances the `./core` submodule and

Phaser's device detection touches `window` under node
(`ReferenceError: window is not defined`, `phaser/src/device/OS.js`). A normal
build therefore leaves a red tree that the dev-push pre-push hook refuses, and
the workaround in use pins core behind the tip.

## Users

- **Game developer in this repo** — must be able to `npm run build` and then
  `npm test` on the resulting pin with both green, without manual
  `git -C core checkout …` gymnastics or offline `engine:sync` fallbacks.

  at the pinned engine, or no work item can reach `in_review` (`implement.py
  finish` runs the build, which re-pins to the tip).

- As a developer, I can run `npm run build` followed by `npm test` on the
  composed pin, and both pass, so I never have to remember the pinned-commit
  workaround.
- As the release line, I can `engine:verify` the recorded pin because the pin

  gitlink at HEAD; the Vitest root preflight no longer aborts every project

  tip, `npm test` (unit + unit-cli via the test skill) passes with **zero**

  is mixed in.

# Transient feedback toasts: readable hold, animate/pause/fade, always on top

**Headline:** Main Street's transient feedback toast (the channel that explains an illegal move, e.g. "Not enough coins to place Bakery") is currently a single 1.1 s pop that starts fading immediately and renders at depth 0, inside the hand band — so it cannot be read and is covered by hand cards. Make it a proper toast: fade/pop in, hold fully opaque for 0.5 s per word, fade out, render above every other scene element, and clear the hand band.

## Problem statement

When a move is refused, the player gets an explanation through `flashError()` → `flashFeedback()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`). The message is created by `popTextOrIcon` with a 1.1 s total lifetime, a fade that begins on the first frame, depth 0, and an anchor at `handY − 20` — which is inside the hand-card row (cards are centred on `handY`, so the top of the cards is `handY − handCardH/2`). The result is text that is too fast to read and is covered by the hand and higher-depth HUD/overlay layers.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "When I make an illegal move, I want to read *why* it was refused without racing the fade or the hand, so I can correct my move instead of guessing."
- **Reduced-motion player:** "I still need the same explanation held for the same readable time, without animation."
- **QA/designer:** "I want the toast's timing and layer to be deterministic and assertable, so a regression is caught by the suite rather than by playing the game."
- **Developer:** "I want one place that owns toast presentation so the feedback channel stays consistent as more messages move into it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Word-based readable hold.** A pure helper (e.g. `feedbackHoldMs(text)`) derives the fully-opaque hold from the message's whitespace-delimited word count: `words × 500 ms` (minimum one word's 500 ms). The toast stays at alpha 1 for exactly that hold between fade-in and fade-out; a 5-word refusal is readable for 2.5 s, not 1.1 s total. Unit tests cover 1, 5 and 10-word messages and empty text.
- [ ] **AC2 — Animate → pause → fade.** Normal presentation runs fade/scale-in (~160 ms), the AC1 fully-opaque pause, then fade-out (~300 ms) before destruction; total lifetime is `fadeIn + hold + fadeOut`. No fade or motion occurs during the pause. Under reduced motion the toast is static at alpha 1 for the same AC1 hold and is then destroyed — no tweens, never dropped. Unit tests assert the sequence, that alpha stays 1 through the hold, and that reduced motion creates no tween.
- [ ] **AC3 — Always above, clear of the hand.** Both the animated and reduced-motion toasts render at a named depth above every Main Street layer (hand cards 0…n, hand panel −100, action row 100, overlays 200–201, stats 900–950, HUD 1000, stats button 1100), e.g. `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000`. The anchor is lifted clear of the hand-card band (`handY − handCardH/2 − margin`) using layout values, with a safe fallback when metrics are missing. Tests assert the applied depth and anchor with the real layout shape.
- [ ] **AC4 — One readable toast, wrapped.** Only one feedback toast is live per scene: a new message destroys the previous toast, cancels its hold/dismiss timers and starts fresh (no stacked duplicates at the same anchor). Long messages word-wrap within the viewport (max width derived from `gameW`) and carry a dark stroke so they stay legible over any background. Tests cover replacement/cancellation and wrap-width selection.
- [ ] **AC5 — Existing feedback contract unchanged.** Message taxonomy (error/confirmation surfaced; guidance/progress dropped), `scene.lastFeedback` / `scene.feedbackHistory`, Activity Log behaviour and the `flashError`/`flashConfirmation` API remain unchanged; the toast is never interactive and never intercepts pointer input. Existing feedback/illegal-afford tests stay green (anchor expectations updated only for the deliberate lift).
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README where relevant, and the VitePress pages under `docs/` (in particular `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel*).
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **In-repo only.** Implement in `src/scenes/` (Main Street). Do **not** edit the engine-owned `core/` submodule or bump the engine pin; the engine's `illegalMoveToast` is a separate component and is not composed by Main Street at this pin.
- **Reduced motion is mandatory.** The in-game setting / `prefers-reduced-motion` path must remain animation-free while preserving the same hold time.
- **No input capture.** The toast is presentation-only; do not make it interactive.
- **Deterministic and testable.** Drive timing through Phaser time/tweens (or an injected clock in tests), never fixed real-time sleeps.
- **Base layout is 1280×720 but expands.** Use layout values (`handY`, `handCardH`, `gameW`, `logX`) rather than new hard-coded pixel positions.
- **Scope is feedback toasts.** Animation-only `popTextOrIcon` effects (income counters, level-up, card-transfer VFX) keep their current short pop; word-based dwell would stall their animation sequences.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline). Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`:
  - `flashFeedback()` records `scene.lastFeedback` / `feedbackHistory`, then uses `duration = options.duration ?? 1100`.
  - Normal path calls `popTextOrIcon({ scene, x, y, label, duration: 1100, riseY: 20, scale: 1.1, reducedMotion: false })`.
  - Reduced-motion path creates `scene.add.text(...).setOrigin(0.5).setDepth(900)` and destroys it after `duration`.
  - `feedbackAnchor(layout)` returns `{ x: logX / 2, y: handY − 20 }`.
- `popTextOrIcon` (`@ui/popTextOrIcon`, engine-owned) runs one tween for the whole duration: `y −20`, `alpha → 0`, `scale 1.1`. There is no pause, and the text has no explicit depth (defaults to 0) or wrap width.
- Depth landscape: hand cards use `depth = index` (0…n), hand panel `−100`, action row `100`, overlays `200–201`, stats `900–950`, HUD `1000`, stats button `1100`. A depth-0 toast therefore sits under hand cards and every HUD/overlay layer.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` mocks `popTextOrIcon` and asserts anchor `{ x: 410, y: 600 }` for `{ logX: 820, handY: 620 }`, plus the reduced-motion static path. `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` asserts `scene.lastFeedback` text for refusals.
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` documents the current 1100 ms `popTextOrIcon` presentation.

## Desired change

1. **Pure timing helper:** `feedbackHoldMs(text: string): number` → `max(1, wordCount) × 500` ms; empty/whitespace text returns 0 (no toast). Export it for tests.
2. **Toast presentation in `MainStreetFeedback`:** create the text at the anchor with `FONT_FAMILY` and the existing 18 px bold white style, origin 0.5, `setDepth(FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH)`, `setWordWrapWidth(min(FEEDBACK_TOAST_MAX_WIDTH, gameW − 40))`, dark stroke, alpha 0/scale 0.9. Fade/scale in over `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_IN_MS`, hold for `feedbackHoldMs(text)`, fade out over `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_OUT_MS`, then destroy. Reduced motion: alpha 1, no tweens, destroy after the hold.
3. **Replacement:** keep at most one toast per scene (module `WeakMap` or a scene field); on a new message, cancel the previous hold timer/tweens and destroy the previous text before showing the new one. Bind scene shutdown/destroy cleanup so no timer or text leaks.
4. **Anchor:** `feedbackAnchor` gains the hand-card height (optional for backward compatibility) and returns `y = handY − handCardH/2 − FEEDBACK_TOAST_MARGIN_PX`; keep the current `logX / 2` horizontal centring and the safe fallback when layout metrics are missing.
5. **Constants:** add `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_IN_MS`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_FADE_OUT_MS`, `FEEDBACK_WORD_HOLD_MS = 500`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_MARGIN_PX`, `FEEDBACK_TOAST_MAX_WIDTH` to `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` (or a small local block if that file is not the right home).
6. **Tests:** rework `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` to assert `feedbackHoldMs`, the fade→hold→fade sequence with a fake scene, alpha 1 during the hold, depth/wrap/anchor, replacement/cancellation, reduced motion with no tweens, and unchanged classification/history. Keep `illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` green.
7. **Docs:** update `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel* (hold formula, sequence, depth, anchor, replacement, reduced motion).

**Order of work (test-first):** write the new timing/presentation tests against the agreed contract, then the helper and constants, then the presentation/replacement and anchor lift, then the docs.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts` — New helper, toast presentation/replacement, anchor lift, reduced-motion path.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — New toast depth, fade/hold/margin/wrap constants if not kept local to the feedback module.
- `tests/main-street/feedback-pop-text.test.ts` — Reworked timing, depth, anchor, replacement and reduced-motion tests.
- `tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts` — Regression: illegal-move reasons still surface through `lastFeedback`.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Update the transient feedback channel presentation contract.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVPWQK3U003DIR6** (completed, `in_review`) — *[Impl] Remove instruction line and route feedback to pop text*: introduced `MainStreetFeedback`, `feedbackAnchor`, `lastFeedback`/`feedbackHistory`, and the 1100 ms `popTextOrIcon` presentation this item replaces.
- **MS-0MVKTB6WS000VLWK** (completed, `in_review`) — *UI simplification when roads are visible*: parent decision that errors/confirmations are surfaced as transient pop text and guidance/progress are dropped (Q4a). This item keeps that taxonomy.
- **CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB** (engine, completed) — *Core illegal-move routine: explain a rejected move with a reason toast*: adds an engine-side `illegalMoveToast` (dwell 2500 ms, depth 1900, y 520). It is **not** composed by Main Street at the pinned engine `0409c1eb`, and `playIllegalFeedback()` does not pass a `reason`; Main Street's visible illegal-move explanation is the `flashError` toast. If the producer intended that engine toast instead, this item must be re-scoped to `~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` plus a Main Street re-pin.
- **MS-0MVQO6N34007DHP8** (critical) — *Bumping the engine pin to core dev tip breaks the unit suite (`phaser window is not defined`)*: relevant only if scope is later widened to the engine toast; it does not block the in-repo feedback toast fix.
- **Docs:** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Transient pop-text feedback channel*; `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (illegal feedback description).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — observed toast is the Main Street feedback channel.** At the pinned engine `0409c1eb`, `shakeIllegalMove` has no `reason` toast and `playIllegalFeedback` passes no reason, so the illegal-move reason the player sees is `flashError` → `flashFeedback` (1100 ms, depth 0, inside the hand band). This exactly matches the report. Research: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:62`, `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts:88`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts:20-64`, `core` gitlink `0409c1eb`.
- **Assumption — scope is feedback toasts only.** `popTextOrIcon` is also used directly for short animation VFX (income `+€`, level-up, card transfer). Those are markers, not explanations; applying a word-based hold would stall animation sequences and is out of scope.
- **Risk — scope creep into the engine toast.** The engine's shared `illegalMoveToast` has the same readability problem (fixed 2500 ms dwell, y 520, depth 1900). It is deliberately not bundled here; record it as a separate engine item and a re-pin if the producer wants it.
- **Risk — long messages linger.** A 20-word reason holds for 10 s. This is the producer's explicit 0.5 s/word rule; the toast is non-interactive and can be replaced by the next message, so it does not block play. No cap is added unless the producer asks for one.
- **Risk — depth above overlays.** `FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000` puts the toast above the stats/help overlays and the HUD. A toast raised while a modal is open will sit over the modal for its bounded lifetime; replacement and auto-dismiss keep that window short. The producer explicitly asked for "above all other elements".
- **Risk — regression in tests pinned to the old anchor.** `feedback-pop-text.test.ts` asserts `y: 600`; the deliberate lift changes that to `handY − handCardH/2 − margin`. Update the assertions with the new contract, do not weaken them.
- **Risk — leaked timers/tweens.** Replacement and scene shutdown must cancel pending hold/fade timers and destroy the text; tests use fake time to prove no callbacks fire after replacement.
- **Assumption — no background panel.** Legibility is achieved with a dark stroke over the text rather than a filled chip; the producer asked for animate/pause/fade/on-top, not a panel. A chip can be added later if the stroke is not enough.
- **Assumption — `duration` option.** No call site passes `FeedbackOptions.duration`; its role is replaced by the word-based hold. To avoid a silent breaking change, keep an optional explicit hold override (renamed `holdMs`) for tests/back-compat and default it to `feedbackHoldMs(text)`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the seed context (too fast, animate/pause/fade, 0.5 s per word, above all elements) plus repository investigation resolved the scope and contract. Each resolution is recorded for producer review.

- Q: "Which toast is the report about — Main Street's feedback pop text or the engine's `illegalMoveToast`?" — Answer (agent, repository investigation): **Main Street's feedback pop text**. Research: the pinned engine is `0409c1eb`, before the engine reason-toast commit `34e0ab6d`; `playIllegalFeedback()` calls `shakeIllegalMove` without a `reason`, so no engine toast is rendered in Main Street. The illegal-move reason is surfaced by `flashError()` (`MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:62`) through `flashFeedback` → `popTextOrIcon` at 1100 ms, depth 0, anchor `handY − 20` (inside the hand band). Source: `git -C core log --all -- src/ui/illegalMoveToast.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetFeedback.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts`.
- Q: "Does 'toasts' include every `popTextOrIcon` call, e.g. income and level-up numbers?" — Answer (agent): **No — feedback toasts only** (`flashFeedback`/`flashError`/`flashConfirmation`). Research: direct `popTextOrIcon` calls are animation VFX with short, self-explanatory labels and are sequenced with board animations; a word-based hold would stall them. Source: `grep -rn popTextOrIcon src/scenes`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § *Event Feedback Animations*.
- Q: "What exactly should 'animate, pause, fade' mean, and how is the 0.5 s/word pause applied?" — Answer (agent): **fade/scale-in ~160 ms → fully opaque hold of `words × 500 ms` → fade-out ~300 ms**; total lifetime is the sum. Reduced motion skips the tweens but keeps the same hold. Source: producer's seed description; implemented contract in AC1/AC2.
- Q: "What does 'above all other elements' mean for layer depth?" — Answer (agent): **a named depth above every Main Street layer** (`FEEDBACK_TOAST_DEPTH = 3000`, above hand cards 0…n, hand panel −100, action 100, overlays 200–201, stats 900–950, HUD 1000, stats button 1100), plus an anchor lifted clear of the hand-card band. - Q: "Should a new message stack with the previous toast or replace it?" — Answer (agent): **replace**. **Type:** bug (regression) · **Priority:** high · **Stage:** intake

## Headline

The ambient reputation crowd is missing again: the pedestrian silhouette layer shipped in v0.1.19 no longer appears on the street in normal play, so reputation has lost its diegetic on-street presence and the reputation income no longer visibly comes from the people in the shops.

## Problem statement

Reputation used to be represented by a live crowd of small silhouettes that walked the roads and entered occupied businesses; those figures scaled with reputation and sourced the end-of-turn reputation income. The producer reports a regression: the crowd is gone. The layer source and its scene/renderer/turn-flow hooks are still present in `dev`, so the regression is most likely in scene integration or rendering (attach/rebuild ordering, camera/mask, HUD refresh path, reducers that gate rendering, or a layout change that moves the layer off-screen) rather than the feature having been deleted.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to see their reputation as a living street: more reputation means a busier street, and the end-of-turn reputation income visibly comes from the people in their shops.
  - *As a player, I want the street to show how reputable I have become, so progress is legible without reading the HUD.*
  - *As a player, I want the people in my shops to be the source of my reputation income, so the economy feels diegetic.*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants the shipped behaviour restored exactly as documented, not redesigned, and wants a guard so this regression cannot silently return.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the layer to stay presentation-only, deterministic, reduced-motion/replay exempt, and non-blocking, and needs a scene-level test that would have caught the disappearance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Regression reproduced and root cause recorded.** The work item records a concrete reproduction (mode, difficulty, steps, build/commit) and the change or condition that made the crowd disappear — the offending commit/file where one exists, or the ruled-out alternatives and the failing condition where it does not. The fix commit references that finding. Verified by reading the work-item comment and the fix commit message.
2. **Crowd is visible in normal play.** On a fresh normal-play game (default settings, not Reduced Motion, not replay/headless), once the HUD has rendered the player's starting reputation the street displays `pedestrianCount(state.resourceBank.reputation)` silhouette figures in `PEDESTRIAN_COLOR`, parented to the live street container. Verified by a scene-level browser/behaviour test that boots the real scene and asserts the layer's live figure count equals the pure helper and that the layer container is attached to the current street container with non-empty, on-screen bounds.
3. **Live population reconciliation still holds.** A reputation gain during a turn fades a figure in and a loss fades a figure out, delta-only, so the on-street count always tracks the HUD reputation value. Verified by the existing live-refresh test plus a scene-level assertion that the count is non-zero and matches `pedestrianCount(reputation)` after the first HUD refresh.
4. **Figures walk the roads and enter occupied businesses.** The documented road-lane walking, nearest-occupied-cell targeting, deliberate (non-teleporting) shop entry and crowd persistence across a street rebuild are retained. Verified by the existing pure/behaviour tests staying green and by a regression assertion that, by the reputation income phase, at least `PEDESTRIAN_MIN_SHOP_RATIO` (25%) of the live crowd is inside occupied cells.
5. **Reputation income is sourced from the crowd.** The `reputation` income phase keeps sourcing each business's coin flight from a figure inside that business (then a figure entering it, then any shopper, then a street anchor — never the HUD reputation counter), with the credited total unchanged. Verified by the existing income-phase source/invariant tests.
6. **Exemptions and determinism preserved.** Reduced Motion and replay/headless modes render no figures, no dissolve and no flights; the layer consumes no gameplay RNG (only the presentation-local PRNG) and a throwing layer never stalls the turn. Verified by existing exemption/determinism tests.
7. **Regression guard added.** A test that fails while the crowd is absent (e.g. a scene-level assertion of a non-empty, attached, visible layer at game start in normal play) is added so a future change cannot silently remove the crowd again. Verified by the new test failing on the pre-fix commit and passing on the fix.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Restore, do not redesign.** The intended behaviour is the one documented in `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Ambient street pedestrians" and delivered by `MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E`; the fix restores it rather than introducing a new crowd design, ratio or choreography.
- **Presentation-only.** The layer and its dissolve must never mutate game state, the transcript or the turn flow; every entry point stays defensive so a bad frame cannot stall a turn.
- **No economy change.** Credited reputation income, the phase-sum invariant and the deferred-mutation handling are untouched.
- **Reduced Motion + replay/headless exemption** remain mandatory.
- **No new gameplay RNG consumption.** Any randomness stays in the presentation-local PRNG.
- **Minimal churn.** Touch only the pedestrian layer and the integration point(s) that caused the regression; do not undo unrelated panel/layout work.
- **Respect repository boundaries.** If the root cause is in the `core` submodule or shared UI, raise a separate core work item and record the dependency rather than editing the submodule silently.

## Existing state

- The feature exists and is wired in `dev`:
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — the layer (`pedestrianCount`, `buildRoadNetwork`, road-lane walking, shop entry, `startNewTurn`, `beginEndOfTurn`, `dissolveIntoCoins`, `setPopulation`, `update`).
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — constructs the layer, destroys it on shutdown and re-clamps it on resize.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — re-attaches the layer at the end of `refreshStreetGrid` after `streetContainer.removeAll(true)`.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — drives `msPedestrians.update(delta)` from the scene `update` loop.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateHudValueChanges` reconciles the population to `pedestrianCount(reputation)`; `dissolveReputationCoins` sources the reputation phase from the layer.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `startNewTurn()` on a new day and `beginEndOfTurn()` at end of turn.
- The feature shipped in **v0.1.19** (epic `MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E`, children listed under Related work).
- Documentation: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Ambient street pedestrians (reputation crowd)" describes the population rule, road walking, shop entry, live refresh, turn lifecycle, income conversion, accessibility and performance.
- The source file is unchanged since v0.1.19, so the regression is expected at an integration point changed after that release.

### Candidate causes to check (investigation starting points, not conclusions)

- **Attach/rebuild ordering:** `refreshStreetGrid` calls `streetContainer.removeAll(true)` (which destroys the layer's container) and re-attaches at the end; a new early return or reordering after v0.1.19 would leave the crowd destroyed.
- **Scene lifecycle:** the layer is re-created in two places in `createScene`; a second construction or a new boot path (new-game overlay, tutorial offer, checkpoint resume) may leave the live instance with `targetCount = 0`.
- **HUD refresh path:** the population is only reconciled from `animateHudValueChanges`; a change that bypasses, early-returns or defers that path (e.g. the display-only counting work) would stop `setPopulation` from running.
- **Render gating:** `isEnabled()` returns false when `replayMode` or `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is true; a settings default change or a mis-detected replay mode would hide the layer.
- **Camera/mask/layout:** pedestrians are map-local children of the masked, camera-transformed street container; a layout, zoom or mask change can move or clip them off-screen while the slots stay visible.
- **Layer stacking:** the "UI simplification when roads are visible" epic made the market, hand and HUD panels opaque and moved the hand band; the crowd may be present but hidden behind a panel rather than absent.
- **End-of-turn timing:** the Turn Summary gate now defers the next day until **[ Next Turn ]**; during that dialog the crowd has already walked off the block, so "empty street" between turns is expected and must be distinguished from an empty street during a turn.

## Desired change

- Diagnose and fix the regression so the ambient reputation crowd is visible during normal play and the documented behaviour (road walking, shop entry, live reconciliation, crowd-sourced reputation income) is restored.
- Add the scene-level regression guard from AC7 so the layer cannot silently disappear again.
- Record the root cause and the guard in the work item and, where the documentation was thin on the lifecycle/attach contract, tighten `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (or add a short note in `src/scenes/README.md`) so the next renderer change has a visible contract.
- Leave the economy, panel treatment, turn pacing and accessibility behaviour untouched.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — the layer; likely unchanged except a defensive fix if the root cause is in the layer.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `refreshStreetGrid` attach ordering / early returns; prime suspect for a rebuild-time disappearance.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — scene `update` loop and `getStreetContainer`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — construction/re-construction, shutdown, resize.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `syncPedestrianPopulation` / `animateHudValueChanges` / `dissolveReputationCoins`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` — animator accessors used by the dissolve path.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `startNewTurn` / `beginEndOfTurn` hooks and the Turn Summary gate.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — pedestrian constants (ratio, colour, size, speed, fade, shop ratio).
- `src/MainStreetMapView.ts` — road bands, viewport rect and camera transform used to place the layer.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — pure/behaviour coverage of the layer.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-live-refresh.test.ts` — live reconciliation coverage.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-count.test.ts` — population rule.
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-reputation-source.test.ts` / `income-phase-reputation-invariant.test.ts` — reputation-phase sourcing and credited-total invariants.
- `tests/main-street/` — new scene-level regression guard (e.g. `pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts`).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — pedestrian layer contract and lifecycle.
- `src/scenes/README.md` — scene module map / layer ownership note.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUYGFVVG009KONJ** (completed) — "Pedestrian count pure helper".

**Decision:** full planning required (effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan`; effort Small, risk High). Approval gate returned `request_approval: false` — approval is only requested for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk, so planning proceeded through the automated review stages without a producer pause.

**Test-first ordering:** both test items (2 and 4) were created before the fix item (3); the guard (2) is unblocked and must be observed red before the fix lands, so the "fails while the crowd is absent" evidence (parent AC7) is captured naturally.

- The root cause is not yet known, so diagnosis is a separate deliverable with its own evidence requirements (reproduction + committed root-cause record) rather than being folded into the fix — the fix item's first AC is "minimal churn at the diagnosed point", which is only checkable once the diagnosis exists.

# Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a signed pack catalogue hosted at a
configured URL to be discovered at runtime and merged into the player's card
pool, so that I can publish packs without rebuilding the game; as a player I
want those packs to show up in my Card Packs panel exactly like bundled packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1 and 6; parent scope items 1, 2, 6;
parent constraints "reuse existing seams", "totality", "additive", "signing key
separation"; locked decisions Q1 and Q2).

## Context

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts every layer once, end-to-end, so the whole
seam is proven before it is hardened. `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` already provides
`PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and adapts a registry to the loader's
`fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` seams, so **no core loader change**
is needed. The remote source is a provider on that registry.

Without this slice there is no usable increment: a signature gate is
inseparable from discovery (an unverified catalogue must never contribute
packs), so verification lands with the first end-to-end path rather than as a
separate layer.

## Scope

1. **Configuration surface.** Read the remote catalogue coordinates from
   `import.meta.env` (`VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL`,
   `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`), validate them, and derive the host
   allow-list. Inert when unset.
2. **Allow-listed bounded fetch primitive.** One total text-fetch helper: refuse
   a host that is not configured (before any request), enforce a hard timeout
   via `AbortController`, map every failure to `null` + one warning.
3. **Signed-manifest verification.** The signed envelope, its deterministic
   canonical payload bytes, pinned-key import from raw base64, and a total
   verifier returning a discriminated result (never throws).
4. **Remote pack source.** `createRemotePackSource(config)` serving
   `<base>/packs/manifest.json` and `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`
   after verification, rejecting the **whole source** on any verification or
   manifest-shape failure.
5. **Composition and boot wiring.** Compose the registry as bundled source
   first, then the remote source; use it on the browser boot path
   (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) without touching the Electron
   content-directory path.

## Design notes

- Ed25519 is available natively in Node 22 WebCrypto and the Playwright
  Chromium used by the browser project — **no new runtime dependency**.
- Verification is memoised per source instance: one manifest fetch and one
  verification per boot, not one per CSV.
- The source's remit is "fetch and refuse only". Merging, precedence and
  duplicate-id rejection stay with the registry and the core merge, which is
  what makes bundled/remote parity automatic.
- Every failure is a warning on the existing logger seam; no UI change
  (decision Q3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` parses and validates `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY` (injectable env for tests) and exposes an allow-list predicate; unset, blank or invalid configuration yields no remote sources and logs a warning rather than throwing.
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` exports the signed envelope type and a deterministic canonical-payload function, plus `verifyPackManifestSignature(...)` returning `ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` / `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable` and never throwing for any input.
- [ ] A manifest signed with the matching private key verifies `ok`; a one-byte body change or a signature from a different keypair returns `invalid-signature`; a blank or absent signature returns `missing-signature`; a non-JSON or wrong-shape envelope returns `malformed-envelope`.
- [ ] The canonical payload is stable under input key reordering so an external operator can reproduce the signed bytes; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A total fetched-text helper refuses a non-configured host **without calling the injected `fetch`**, and maps timeout, rejection, non-2xx and body-read failure to `null` with one warning.
- [ ] A `createRemotePackSource(config)` factory returns a `PackSource` whose `id` distinguishes it from the bundled source, serving `manifest.json` and `<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv` from the configured base once the manifest verifies.
- [ ] A remote pack served by a fake transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merged pool with its cards and reaches the Card Packs listing input; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A missing, invalid, non-pinned-key or malformed manifest makes **every** path from that source resolve `null`, logs exactly one source-level warning, and never throws.
- [ ] The remote source never throws for any input (invalid config, non-string path, empty path, throwing transport), asserted by a table-driven test.
- [ ] `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` composes the configured remote source on the browser path, while an explicit launcher `contentDir` composes no remote source and performs no remote fetch (asserted with a spy).
- [ ] No new entry is added to `package.json` dependencies.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, composition
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — boot wiring on the browser path
- `./env.d.ts` — declared env vars
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDiscovery.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackIntegrity.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`

## Deliverables

- The end-to-end discovery path: configured URL → verified manifest → served
  CSV → merged pool → listing.
- The configuration, verifier and fetch primitives the later slices harden.
- Signed-manifest fixtures (keypair generation, signing, tampering, fake
  transport) reused by the verification items.
